All four files read (plus the vllm `README.md` and `run.sh` for the glue). Here's the end-to-end flow of a vLLM benchmark run.

## The four roles

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` | The rules: repo map + iron rules (provenance, versioning, VRAM gating, depth curves) that every run must satisfy |
| `docs/GUIDE.md` | Operator manual: step-by-step for both tracks; its vLLM section (3) shows the old raw-docker boot, superseded by the profile launcher |
| `serve_vllm.sh` | **Server side** — profile-driven, reproducible boot of a vLLM Docker image; waits for health; records provenance |
| `capture_engine.py` | **Measurement side** — the one prober; streams OpenAI-compatible `/v1` and records every measurable signal |

The glue between them: `run.sh` (single comparison) / `campaign.sh` (matrix, resumable), `profiles/<engine>/*.env`, `report.py` (charts), and the `/benchmark-results` skill (write-up).

## Phase 1 — Boot the server (`serve_vllm.sh start`)

**1. Profile selection** — `PROFILE=sly-radiance/qwen38-mxfp4` resolves to two layers:
- `profiles/sly-radiance/qwen38-mxfp4.env` (model layer): `MODEL_DIR` (pinned HF snapshot at `…/models/<org>__<repo>@<rev>`), `SERVED_NAME`, `MAXLEN`, `MODEL_ENV` (e.g. all the `RADIANCE_MXFP4_*` switches), `MODEL_ARGS` (e.g. `--quantization quark`).
- `profiles/sly-radiance/_engine.env` (engine layer): `IMAGE` (digest-pinned `ghcr.io/slybase/vllm-sly-radiance:1.6.0-rocm10.1`), `GPU_UTIL`, `MAXSEQS`, `KV_DTYPE`, `FREE_MIB_FLOOR`, `CACHE_MOUNTS` (root-cache/triton/aiter → per-image-tag host dirs), `ENGINE_ENV` (HIP visible devices, `RADIANCE_RUN_BWTEST=0`), `ENGINE_ARGS` (the full `vllm serve` flag set: `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `--enable-prompt-tokens-details`, `--enable-force-include-usage`, chat template, `--override-generation-config`, …).

Sourced model-first, engine-second; every engine knob is `${VAR:-default}`, so **command line > model profile > engine profile**.

**2. Contract check** (every mode, including `print` — exits 2 naming each violation before any docker call): required scalars, integer checks, the five arrays must be declared as arrays, and the **chat-template silence rule** — either `--chat-template` in args, `CHAT_TEMPLATE=<host .jinja>` (mounted ro at `/templates/`, replacing the profile's value), or `CHAT_TEMPLATE_NONE="<reason>"`. An image missing the template fails only at first request, so silence is an error.

**3. Optional overrides** — `KVCACHE=ram` splices Sly's GPU→RAM prefix-cache tier verbatim: 6 `RADIANCE_*` patches applied at container start (mixed-hit fatal, rest warn), `RADIANCE_*` env switches, `--kv-offloading-size/--kv-offloading-backend native`, and a larger `--shm-size` (tier + 16g). `DRAFT_DIR` mounts a speculative drafter; `EXTRA_ARGS` appends.

**4. Pre-boot conditions** (iron rule 14):
- `MODEL_DIR/config.json` exists (and `DRAFT_DIR/config.json` if set);
- image present, or `AUTO_PULL=1` pulls once;
- no stale container, port free (127.0.0.1 only);
- **free-VRAM floor**: `start` mode runs `bench/lib/gpu_exclusive.sh $FREE_MIB_FLOOR` (unloads llama-swap, kills the hipfire shape, fails loudly naming the holder); `run` mode (for llama-swap, foreground `--rm`) waits up to `FLOOR_WAIT` for the previous model's VRAM to drain, then refuses below floor.

**5. Launch + watchdog** — `docker run` with `--device /dev/kfd /dev/dri`, numeric render/video GIDs, `--shm-size`, model mount ro, `$HF_CACHE:/hf` (in-container HF fetches land on the shared host), per-tag cache mounts, all env/args. A **watchdog** polls sysfs free-VRAM every 0.2 s and `docker kill`s the container if free VRAM drops below `WATCHDOG_MIB` (default 256) during boot — the 2026-10-22 NVFP4 requant filled the card to 24 MiB free and killed the desktop session 22 s later; `--gpu-memory-utilization` does not bound the load phase, so the watchdog is the only thing that can.

**6. Health gate + provenance** — up to `WAIT` (1200 s; first boot compiles) seconds of `curl /health`; then it verifies `/v1/models` actually serves `SERVED_NAME` (aborts if a different model answers), and records `vllm_version` + `up_after_s`. Every boot writes `bench/.servers/<port>.cmdline`: the exact docker argv, image digest, model repo+revision (from `SOURCE.txt`), start time. This is what iron rule 2 (reproducibility) and iron rule 1 (provenance) consume later.

## Phase 2 — Drive the server (`run.sh` / `campaign.sh`)

`run.sh` (the single-comparison path) does:
1. Create `bench/runs/<stamp>-engine-<slug>/`, write `meta.txt` (date, workload, max_tokens, concurrency, reps, prefix mode, or conversation params), copy the prompt files in.
2. Optionally start `vram_sampler.py` in the background (`SAMPLE_VRAM=1`) → `gpu_samples.csv` (wait for its init so a fast probe can't kill it).
3. For each engine in `ENGINES` (`label|url|model` — for vLLM: `vllm|http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1|qwen38-27b-mxfp4`): health-check, record `/props` and `/models` (vLLM's `/props` is empty — that's `|| true`), snap vLLM's speculative counters via `spec_metrics.py`, then invoke the prober:
   - `probe` mode: `capture_engine.py probe --url … --prompt-file … --max-tokens … --concurrency … --reps … --warmup … --prefix-mode … --api … --engine … --label …` → `results.jsonl`
   - `MODE=conversation`: `capture_engine.py conversation … --start-tokens … --step-tokens … --max-depth …` → `results.jsonl`
4. Stop the sampler; fold the GPU memory summary into `results.jsonl` as a `gpu` row (peak VRAM / peak GTT / load-time VRAM / avg power) and `phase_power.py` into `power` rows (prefill vs decode power, joined on the probe's wall-clock phase boundaries).
5. Print the aggregate rows; exit 1 if any probe failed (so a caller can't mark an all-failed run as done).

`campaign.sh` is the same plumbing in a matrix: restart the server per config (different profile/depth/concurrency), resumable, continue-on-fail.

## Phase 3 — Measure (`capture_engine.py`)

One streaming core (`stream()`) serves all modes: it POSTs to `/chat/completions` or `/completions` with `stream: true` + `stream_options: include_usage`, and parses SSE chunks capturing:
- `ttft` (first token), `ttfa` (first answer token — after `reasoning_content` deltas or `</think>`),
- `usage` (prompt/completion/cached tokens — vLLM's `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` and `--enable-force-include-usage` are what make `cached_tokens` available),
- `timings` (llama.cpp's block; **vLLM doesn't send it**, so the prober falls back to wall-clock deltas: `decode = (gen-1)/(total-ttft)`, `prefill = prompt_tokens/ttft`),
- `finish_reason`, and both reasoning styles (a separate `reasoning_content` field, or inline `…` in content).

**`probe` mode** (the throughput track): reads the prompt file(s), applies prefix mode (`none`/`unique`/`shared`/`tail` — `tail` = shared body + divergent tail, the realistic agentic partial-cache pattern), runs `warmup` untimed requests, then `reps` waves of `concurrency` barrier-synchronized threads. One `{kind:"request"}` line per request (ttft, ttfa, decode/prefill tok/s, gen/prompt tokens, wall-clock phase boundaries for the power join) + one `{kind:"aggregate"}` line (ttft p50/p95, decode p50, prefill p50, aggregate_tok/s, n_err).

**`conversation` mode** (iron rule 17 — context capacity ≠ per-request prefill size): turn 0 sends `--start-tokens` of the source file; each later turn appends the model's reply + `--step-tokens` more (or a `--turn-prompt` task), prior turns cached server-side, until `--max-depth`. Each turn emits a `{kind:"turn"}` line with `context_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `prefill_new_tok_s` (new tokens / ttft — not full-prompt/ttft, which would count cached tokens), decode, ttft, wall-clock phases, and `kv_usage_peak` — polled by `_kv_poller` from **vLLM's `vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc`** in `/metrics` *during* the turn (the gauge counts blocks held by running requests, so it must be read while in flight; null on engines without it). An errored or cut-stream turn (no `finish_reason`) is recorded as an error and ends its conversation — iron rule 18 (an interrupted run is not a result).

**`tasks` mode** (quality track): one task at a time, full response + think/answer split + health flags, for the graders.

**vLLM-specific adaptations** in the prober: `count_tokens()` tries vLLM's `/tokenize` shape (`{"prompt"}` → `{"count"}`); the `timings` fallback above; the KV-gauge poller; `--enable-prompt-tokens-details`/`--enable-force-include-usage` on the server side (in `ENGINE_ARGS`) are what make `cached_tokens` and `usage` arrive at all.

## Phase 4 — Report (CLAUDE.md's documentation rules)

- `report.py <run_dir>` → theme-aware SVG `charts/` + `appendix.md` (depth curves, concurrency scaling, TTFT p95, memory row); failures are surfaced, never averaged in.
- `/benchmark-results` skill → `campaigns/<date>-<slug>/analysis.md` (or `docs/analysis/<stamp>-<slug>.md`), summary + table first, **memory column mandatory**, Legend, Consequences & root causes each tagged MEASURED/CLAIMED/INFERRED (iron rule 1), registered in `docs/INDEX.md`.

## Where the CLAUDE.md rules bind the flow

- **Iron rule 14** (gate on free VRAM as a precondition): `gpu_exclusive.sh` in `start` mode / the floor-wait in `run` mode; the watchdog covers the boot phase the floor can't.
- **Iron rule 2** (reproducibility): `bench/.servers/<port>.cmdline` (argv + image digest + model revision + vllm_version) + `run.sh`'s `meta.txt` + `props`/`models` files.
- **Iron rule 7** (VRAM: measure, never calculate): the `gpu` row from `vram_sampler.py`, never the `--gpu-memory-utilization` estimate.
- **Iron rule 16** (depth is a variable): the depth campaign (4+ cold depths + `conversation` mode) is what produces the decay exponent, not a single point.
- **Iron rule 17** (context capacity ≠ per-request prefill size): `conversation` mode exists precisely for this.
- **Iron rule 18** (interrupted run ≠ result): cut-stream detection in `run_conversation`, error rows in `run_tasks`, `run.sh`'s exit-1 on probe failure.

One note: `GUIDE.md`'s vLLM section (3) still shows the old raw `docker run` boot and the "27B failed to load / 35B AWQ only" caveat — the current path is the profile-driven `serve_vllm.sh` (per `vllm/README.md`, stress-tested and smoke-booted 2026-10-22, with the baseline + DFlash2 campaigns already done). If you want, I can update that section to point at the launcher.
